lessons: This review resolves two forecasts, and they point in OPPOSITE directions relative to the Avoid -- adjudicated by name, not averaged away. (1) The FQ1 FY27 revenue miss (INR 6,951M vs the ~INR 7,340.9M bar) CONFIRMS the earnings-deceleration forecast and supports the Avoid. (2) A further CFO exit (Raghavan out effective 20-Aug-2026, Ritolia in) FALSIFIES the 'no further exit' forecast and fires kill criterion 7 -- also supporting the Avoid, since the forecast being wrong here means the governance risk deepened exactly as the thesis warned it might.

Against those two confirming facts, the price and margin trend cut the other way: HCG is up 10.5% since the decision price (7.6 points ahead of NIFTY 50) and Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin (19.4% vs 18.2%) and adjusted PAT (+190% YoY) both improved. This is early, partial evidence for exactly the false-negative scenario the pre-mortem's single highest-severity kill-criteria attack named: the ramping-centre cohort migrating toward the mature ~27%-ROCE bucket faster than modelled. thesis_status is 'at-risk' because of this genuine tension, not because either side has been disproven.

The audited-FY26-PAT forecast is NOT resolved this review despite tempting secondary-source language ('25% increase in FY26 net profit to INR 557 Mn'). Per CLAUDE.md source-hierarchy discipline, an aggregator's paraphrase is not sufficient to determine whether this is the audited statutory figure reconciling to the adjusted number, or the same adjusted figure being restated. This is deliberately left 'still open' rather than resolved on a weak source -- the correct next step is the primary Annual Report, not another web search.

A material discrepancy surfaced and is flagged rather than silently reconciled: this review's source describes the Milann/BACC divestment consideration as ~INR 376.4M total (~INR 282.3M received 29-Jun-2026), materially smaller than the ~INR 632M EV figure the 30d review carried. Both figures are web-sourced; neither has been checked against the primary sale agreement or exchange filing.

Rights issue: HCG completed a rights issue raising INR 4,250M (oversubscribed 1.3x) -- a fact not contemplated in the original 2026-06-01 thesis at all. This changes the share count the per-share (EPS, ROIC) forecasts were built on and needs to be folded into the next earnings/valuation work, not left as an unstated distortion in the comparison base.

Price fields: review_price (~INR 714, sourced 2026-08-26) is about a week stale relative to the review date; no more current figure was found. NIFTY 50 benchmark levels (23,382.60 on 2026-06-01; 24,055.80 on 2026-09-01) are a reasonable but not exact match to the entry_price_timestamp ('2026-05, late-May 2026 pool snapshot'). sector_return_pct is left null: no NIFTY Healthcare level near the decision date could be sourced with a matching date, only percentage-move commentary for unrelated days -- publishing an unmatched-basis sector return here would be exactly the kind of mismatched-basis defect CLAUDE.md §15 exists to prevent.

Single most important takeaway: two of the three concrete facts that resolved this quarter deepen the Avoid (the revenue miss, the further CFO exit); the third (the margin/price move) is the specific false-negative risk the pre-mortem itself named as the way this call could be wrong. Both must be watched into the FY26 audited annual report and the FQ2 FY27 print, not resolved by picking a side now.

pre_mortem_check.notes: Genuinely mixed, not a clean vindication or contradiction -- deviating from the mechanical table with this explanation, as its rules allow. Two of the three concrete facts that resolved this quarter deepen the Avoid case (the FQ1 revenue miss confirms the earnings-deceleration forecast; a further CFO exit fires kill criterion 7, exactly the governance risk the thesis flagged). But the pre-mortem's own single highest-severity kill_criteria_attack item -- 'West-cluster utilisation climbs toward South's ~68% / ramp converts' (severity: high) -- is showing early, partial support: adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 19.4% from 18.2%, adjusted PAT rose 190% YoY, and the stock has re-rated 10.5% above the decision price (7.6 points ahead of NIFTY 50) in the same quarter. Calling this cleanly 'contradicted' would overstate how far the ramp thesis has actually progressed on one quarter of data; calling it 'vindicated' would ignore the confirmed CFO exit and revenue miss. thesis_status is 'at-risk' precisely because of this unresolved tension.

memo_delta.summary: Real news this quarter, cutting both ways. Against that, Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin and adjusted PAT both improved materially, the Milann/BACC divestment closed, a rights issue raised INR 4,250M, and the stock has risen 10.5% since the decision price (7.6 points ahead of NIFTY 50) -- early, partial evidence for the pre-mortem's own flagged false-negative scenario. memo_delta.stage_one_comment: Real news on HealthCare Global this quarter, and it cuts both ways. First quarter revenue for the year came in at 6.95 billion rupees, up 13 percent, below the roughly 7.34 billion rupee bar we were watching, which confirms our earnings-deceleration view. Separately, the company had another CFO change, with Srinivasa Raghavan leaving on 20 August and Ruby Ritolia named to replace him, which is a real deepening of the governance concern we already flagged as a top risk. Against that, adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 19.4 percent from 18.2, adjusted profit nearly tripled off a small base, the fertility business sale closed, a rights issue raised 4.25 billion rupees, and the stock is up about 10.5 percent since our note versus roughly 2.9 percent for the Nifty 50. That improvement is exactly the risk our own red-team flagged as the way this Avoid could be wrong: the newer hospitals ramping up faster than we modelled. We are not changing the rating. Two of three concrete facts this quarter support staying away; the third is a real, early warning sign worth taking seriously, not dismissing. The audited profit figure for the full year still needs checking against the actual annual report, not press coverage.
